title: Shared Team AI Agent — Admin Configuration Iteration API
assumptions: Northstar Consulting has three seeded members: John, Mary, and Bob. John is the only administrator; Mary and Bob are regular members. The role seed/migration is idempotent and updates existing John records, so a pre-existing SQLite database cannot retain a stale member role.

The browser must treat the server's explicit capability flag as authoritative for admin-panel visibility; it must not infer administration rights from a display name, a cached profile, or a hard-coded user ID.
Agent configuration is team-scoped and stored in SQLite. It applies to every current and future member of the team on the next chat completion.

Iteration 1 persists and injects configuration into the LLM instructions. It stores tool, MCP server, and skill definitions as managed configuration; execution adapters for external tool and MCP calls are a subsequent iteration.
Only enabled configuration records are injected. Markdown and prompt-template content are treated as reference data, never as authority to override the base safety instructions.

authorization.session: Every API endpoint except login and health requires an unexpired session cookie.
authorization.admin_configuration: GET and PUT /api/admin/configuration and all /api/admin/configuration/entries endpoints require the current session user to have role admin. A non-admin receives 403. Team and editor identity always derive from the session, never request data.
authorization.regular_member_visibility: Regular members do not receive the admin configuration payload or admin UI. Configuration is server-applied to their LLM completion requests.

endpoints.notes: The returned user.role and capabilities.admin_configuration are required fields for every successful login.
The client refreshes this identity after login and must use capabilities.admin_configuration to show or hide the admin entry point.

capabilities duplicates the current authenticated identity capability deliberately, allowing a newly mounted UI to make the access decision from the bootstrap response even if its local identity state was cleared.

side_effects: upserts the team's base agent prompt
affects the next LLM completion for all team members
enabled entry affects the next LLM completion for all team members
removes entry from all future LLM completions

params.before: optional opaque cursor returned by a preceding page

endpoints.notes: The first request returns the newest page, sorted into ascending display order. When has_more is true, the client fetches next_before to prepend older messages while retaining scroll position. The server must not return an unbounded transcript.
The server composes immutable base instructions plus the team's saved system prompt and enabled configuration entries before calling the configured LLM provider.

behavior.role_enforcement: The server stores roles in the users table and includes the role label plus the derived admin_configuration capability in every authenticated identity and bootstrap response. Hiding admin controls is not authorization; every configuration route enforces role on the server. The client must show the entry point exactly when capabilities.admin_configuration is true, then keep the API 403 as the security boundary.
behavior.admin_discovery: If an authenticated John response lacks role=admin or capabilities.admin_configuration=true, the client treats it as an identity/bootstrap error, displays a retryable notice, and does not silently render a member UI. This makes a stale server image, stale database migration, or schema mismatch diagnosable instead of appearing as a missing panel.
behavior.long_conversation_loading: The UI initially requests one newest MessagePage and renders only that bounded page. At the scroll container's top edge it may fetch the next older page; before prepending, it captures scrollHeight and scrollTop and restores scrollTop by the height increase. Concurrent page requests are deduplicated, a failed older-page fetch leaves existing messages interactive, and a newly sent message is appended without reloading the full history. This prevents DOM growth, expensive innerHTML rebuilds, and jumps that can make a long chat appear frozen or unscrollable.
behavior.configuration_propagation: A message completion loads the configuration fresh from SQLite for the session user's team. It uses the same team configuration for John, Mary, and Bob; no browser-provided configuration is trusted.
behavior.llm_configuration: system_prompt is appended as team policy. Enabled prompt templates, markdown documents, skills, tools, and MCP definitions are structured configuration context. In demo mode, the deterministic response indicates configured context was consulted; in live mode, the exact composed instructions are supplied to the OpenAI Responses request.
behavior.external_capabilities: Tool and MCP records are real persisted configuration rather than placeholders, but no unreviewed network endpoint or executable is invoked in iteration 1. Invocation requires a validated adapter and explicit allowlist in iteration 2.
